Ultra Force.name: Ultra Force
Ultra Force.basicInfo: Tokyo's premier licensed hero organization and the authority overseeing Chikara Academy, hero operations, public safety, and the Blacklisted redemption program.
Ultra Force.hiddenInfo: Ultra Force's public hero mission is genuine, but internal departments disagree over surveillance, rehabilitation, acceptable force, and how much autonomy former villains deserve.

Chikara Academy.name: Chikara Academy
Chikara Academy.basicInfo: A prestigious superhero university that trains students in rescue, support, combat, investigation, media, and agency operations.
Chikara Academy.hiddenInfo: Faculty members quietly track student rivalries, stress, power instability, villain-path risks, and the possibility that some students may reject hero society.

Blacklisted Redemption Program.name: Blacklisted Redemption Program
Blacklisted Redemption Program.basicInfo: An Ultra Force redemption program giving former villains structured housing, training, field missions, medical support, and conditional freedom throughout Tokyo while preserving a path toward legitimate hero status. It also runs a controversial anti-Turned task force that hunts, captures, evaluates, and sometimes attempts to rehabilitate suspected Turned targets.
Blacklisted Redemption Program.hiddenInfo: Blacklisted members are not under constant surveillance. They can travel around Tokyo, visit ordinary locations, pursue personal activities, and choose from approved opportunities between assignments. Their freedom remains conditional: they must complete assigned objectives, obey emergency safety orders, respect legal restrictions, and report mission results afterward. The anti-Turned task force uses warrants, intelligence, informants, and field teams, but its evidence can be incomplete or biased. Some hunters want public safety; others exploit fear of Turned people for power. Restrictions can tighten after serious misconduct, escape attempts, refusal of mandatory objectives, or threats to public safety.

Kurokawa Underworld.name: Kurokawa Underworld
Kurokawa Underworld.basicInfo: A loose network of criminals, fixers, smugglers, nightlife operators, debt collectors, and information brokers controlling hidden commerce in Kurokawa Ward. Its most influential hub is The Velvet Lantern, whose owner's legitimate businesses and civic reputation conceal a web of debt, favors, political leverage, and criminal intermediaries.
Kurokawa Underworld.hiddenInfo: The underworld is divided into competing circles; some exploit residents, some protect their neighborhoods, and some are willing to negotiate with heroes or former villains.

Obsidian Crown Agency.name: Obsidian Crown Agency
Obsidian Crown Agency.basicInfo: A fortified supervillain agency behind a legal security-consultancy front. It coordinates powered criminals, illicit experiments, political protection, covert sabotage, and high-risk assassination contracts for targets considered dangerous, unstable, disloyal, or too messy to leave active.
Obsidian Crown Agency.hiddenInfo: Obsidian Crown keeps separate records for public clients, criminal partners, coerced workers, and protected targets. The agency offers more dangerous contracts than Nightshade: assassinations of gang leaders, rival criminals, pro heroes, corrupt officials, witnesses, defectors, unstable assets, or criminals whose behavior attracts unwanted attention. Other work may involve surveillance, infiltration, impersonation, sabotage, kidnapping, intimidation, targeted destruction, or nonlethal extraction. Target dossiers may be incomplete or deliberately deceptive. Accepting a contract can create legal, faction, reputation, civilian, and retaliation consequences. Players may refuse, negotiate, expose the client, switch to capture, rescue the target, betray the agency, or abandon the contract. The agency considers a target messy when they destabilize criminal networks, betray agreements, create excessive public attention, threaten long-term plans, or become impossible to control.

Villain Empire Network.name: Villain Empire Network
Villain Empire Network.basicInfo: An emerging criminal network built on recruitment, territory, illicit income, information, and alliances, open to villains and criminals who join or ally with it.
Villain Empire Network.hiddenInfo: Its structure is not predetermined: it can become disciplined, theatrical, exploitative, protective, or collapse under rival pressure depending on the choices of those who build and join it.

Tokyo Curse Squad.name: Tokyo Curse Squad
Tokyo Curse Squad.basicInfo: A hidden Old Tokyo team made up of people with Cursed Item, Magical Power, and Supernatural power types. The Tokyo Curse Squad protects its neighborhoods, preserves old pacts, contains dangerous artifacts, and distrusts institutions that try to classify or weaponize the supernatural.
Tokyo Curse Squad.hiddenInfo: The Tokyo Curse Squad is not unified. Cursed-item wielders, magical practitioners, supernatural beings, traditional guardians, spirits, and ambitious ritualists disagree about secrecy, hero licensing, forbidden magic, and whether modern power society can be trusted. Anyone may seek membership regardless of origin or prior affiliation, except current Blacklisted members, who are barred from joining the squad. Membership is optional: a character may join, remain an ally, decline, or leave later. The squad and its NPCs remain part of the shared Chikara Tokyo universe and may cross paths with characters from any background.

Nightshade Exchange.name: Nightshade Exchange
Nightshade Exchange.basicInfo: A global criminal contract marketplace that sells protection rackets, shakedowns, debt collection, intimidation, theft, gang theft, sabotage, extortion, territory pressure, fencing, retaliation, extraction, information, crew hire, and other villain work to powered and non-powered operators. Security and courier work exist as fronts or supporting jobs, not as its defining identity.
Nightshade Exchange.hiddenInfo: Nightshade's encrypted app is easy for new players to discover through rumors, dead drops, invite links, or anonymous signup. Listings are divided into street pressure, theft and recovery, organization-level control, high-risk criminal contracts, and crew recruitment. Players may hire temporary crews for gang jobs, surveillance, intimidation, theft, protection, sabotage, transport, extraction, territory pressure, or a larger operation. Each crew listing identifies the crew's skills, size, cost, loyalty, availability, reputation, heat, required payment, expected split, territory, and likely consequences. Crews are NPCs with their own motives, competence, loyalty, fear, rivalries, and refusal conditions; they are not disposable units and may abandon, betray, renegotiate, panic, get arrested, or demand more after complications. Hiring a crew never guarantees success. Typical jobs include demanding protection payments from businesses, shaking down venues, collecting debts, stealing money or contraband from rival gangs, burglarizing private or commercial targets, sabotaging supplies, forcing territory recognition, fencing stolen goods, retaliating against leaks, and taking over weakened criminal operations. Each listing gives estimated payment, location, danger, legality, civilian risk, required skills, and whether powers are expected, but the app does not guarantee safety, payment, truthfulness, or anonymity. Some listings are scams, traps, rival tests, or bait-and-switch jobs. Players may refuse, negotiate, investigate the client, choose surveillance or extraction instead, expose the broker, betray the network, or leave. Nightshade rewards fear, profit, leverage, and control; visible violence, civilian harm, betrayal, and territorial overreach create heat and retaliation.

Misfit Hero Agency.name: Misfit Hero Agency
Misfit Hero Agency.basicInfo: A licensed but black-sheep hero agency operating from a rundown storefront on Hero Agency Row. The agency accepts low-prestige, politically awkward, dangerous, and poorly funded assignments that larger organizations avoid. Its team lives and works together around daily dispatches, rescues, investigations, training, and improvised found-family routines.
Misfit Hero Agency.hiddenInfo: Senior hero institutions use the Misfit Hero Agency as a pressure valve for difficult assignments while publicly dismissing its reputation. The agency's director protects its license and staff as best they can. The agency can offer its members and contractors daily jobs, emergency calls, training, reputation work, internal disputes, and cross-faction cases involving police, heroes, civilians, and criminal groups. Membership is optional and does not force loyalty, friendship, romance, or residence.

Metropolitan Police.name: Metropolitan Police
Metropolitan Police.basicInfo: Tokyo's metropolitan police organization responsible for public safety, investigations, emergency response, evidence handling, patrol operations, and lawful cooperation with licensed heroes. Its officers handle ordinary crime and powered incidents through procedure, jurisdiction, de-escalation, accountability, and coordinated response.
Metropolitan Police.hiddenInfo: The Metropolitan Police is internally divided over how much authority powered officers and licensed heroes should have during emergencies. It can offer its officers patrols, investigations, apartment calls, evidence follow-ups, witness interviews, emergency backup requests, training requirements, and internal-affairs complications. Membership is optional and does not force permanent loyalty or agreement with police policy.

Backstreet Vigilantes.name: Backstreet Vigilantes
Backstreet Vigilantes.basicInfo:
The network has no single headquarters. Couriers, lookout posts, rooftop routes, abandoned service spaces, and trusted businesses connect small cells. Members protect identities and share information selectively. Their current work focuses on gang hideouts and the people harmed by them.

Description: A loose anti-establishment network operating through Tokyo's backstreets, rooftops, shuttered storefronts, and improvised safehouses. They believe the licensed hero system protects its reputation before it protects vulnerable people. Members expose corruption, disrupt predatory gangs, extract civilians, and dismantle gang hideouts using intimidation, sabotage, ambushes, and controlled nonlethal force. The core members are bound by a hard no-kill rule. They may use dangerous force to stop an immediate threat, but they do not intentionally kill, execute, or accept lethal methods as operational policy. The faction remains morally gray and distrustful of official heroes and police, while insisting that protecting civilians includes refusing to become executioners.
Goals: Dismantle gang hideouts and predatory criminal operations. Protect backstreet residents overlooked by official institutions. Expose failures, corruption, and cover-ups within the current hero system. Build enough local trust and leverage to operate independently.
Values: Civilian protection. Mutual aid. Accountability outside official institutions. Operational secrecy. Results over public approval. Hard no-kill rule. Nonlethal restraint and rescue.
Default quest themes: Gang hideout surveillance and nonlethal takedowns. Civilian extraction and protection. Evidence gathering against criminal or institutional abuse. Rooftop courier work and safehouse coordination. Internal disputes over escalation and restraint.
Backstreet Vigilantes.hiddenInfo:
Conflicts: Police and licensed heroes may treat them as criminals. Their forceful methods can endanger civilians and destroy evidence. The core members disagree about restraint, risk, and how far to push a nonlethal takedown. The no-kill rule is tested by revenge, hostage situations, villains who threaten mass harm, and mistaken intelligence. Mistaken intelligence can turn a rescue mission into an attack on the wrong people.
Recruitment: Recruits are approached through demonstrated courage, useful information, local trust, or survival under pressure. The faction does not accept every applicant and may test whether a prospect can protect civilians without turning violence into personal gratification.

Kurokawa Street Syndicate.name: Kurokawa Street Syndicate
Kurokawa Street Syndicate.basicInfo:
A street-level criminal network rooted in Kurokawa District and connected to crews across Central Tokyo and Tokyo Bay. The Syndicate is held together by money, fear, favors, protection payments, blackmail, and controlled access to illegal work. Its unseen kingpin rarely needs to appear personally; lieutenants, minor powered villains, fixers, and ordinary thugs enforce the network's interests block by block.

Description: The Kurokawa Street Syndicate presents itself as practical neighborhood power. It offers protection where official institutions are slow, then manufactures the danger that makes protection necessary. Some members are opportunistic criminals, some are coerced, and some believe the Syndicate provides stability. Its operations create constant pressure on shops, residents, transport workers, vulnerable powered people, and rival criminal crews.
Goals: Control protection and illicit commerce in Kurokawa District. Expand influence through Central Tokyo and Tokyo Bay connections. Acquire money, information, contraband, and leverage over local businesses. Recruit or control minor powered villains and useful specialists. Keep police, heroes, vigilantes, and rival gangs reacting to separate incidents.
Values: Loyalty rewarded through access and protection. Silence and information discipline. Profit before pride. Fear as a practical tool. Reciprocity when useful.
Roles: Kingpin-style leader, Lieutenants, Minor powered crew leaders, Thugs and enforcers, Lookouts and couriers, Fixers and informants, Drivers and smugglers, Bookkeepers and intermediaries
Territory: Kurokawa District backstreets. Central Tokyo service routes and nightlife corridors. Tokyo Bay logistics yards, warehouses, and waterfront contacts.
Quest themes: Take down or investigate a gang hideout. Protect a business from an escalating protection racket. Recover stolen cargo or support equipment. Find a missing courier, witness, or coerced lookout. Expose a blackmail ledger or payment route. Interrupt an underground fight or illegal gambling operation. Rescue someone being held for debt or leverage. Track a shipment through alleys, rooftops, stations, or the waterfront. Turn a lieutenant against the network through evidence or negotiation. Survive retaliation after disrupting a Syndicate operation.
Kurokawa Street Syndicate.hiddenInfo:
Structure: The Syndicate is divided into small crews so that no ordinary member understands the entire network. Thugs and lookouts handle street pressure. Minor powered villains lead specialized crews or serve as feared enforcers. Fixers manage money, transport, forged access, information, and safe locations. Lieutenants collect payments, settle disputes, and report upward. The kingpin-style leader controls priorities through intermediaries and deniable orders.
Crimes: Protection rackets against ramen shops, bars, clinics, landlords, and small businesses. Extortion, intimidation, debt collection, and blackmail. Smuggling weapons, illegal support gear, stolen goods, and contraband. Operating gang hideouts, stash houses, and temporary holding sites. Recruiting vulnerable powered people through money, threats, debt, or promises of belonging. Coercing lookouts, couriers, drivers, informants, and residents. Robbery, burglary, cargo theft, and hijacking of valuable deliveries. Illegal gambling, underground fights, and rigged betting. Kidnapping or unlawful detention when leverage is considered valuable. Witness intimidation, evidence destruction, arson, and retaliatory property damage. Disinformation and rumor campaigns against rivals, police, heroes, and vigilantes. Paying corrupt intermediaries and exploiting institutional failures.
Methods: Use intimidation, surveillance, bribery, sabotage, ambushes, extortion, false reports, staged disputes, targeted violence, and controlled escalation. Do not make every member combat-ready or every encounter a fight. Thugs are usually Trivial or Weak individually; powered crew leaders are generally Average or Strong according to role; the leader's personal threat should be established separately by the leader NPC. Make serious danger legible and preserve options such as negotiation, evidence gathering, escape, civilian protection, calling authorities, turning informants, or attacking the network's logistics.
Conflicts: Backstreet Vigilantes challenge the Syndicate's control of Kurokawa. Police and licensed heroes pursue the network but may lack evidence or jurisdiction. Rival gangs compete for routes, businesses, and powered recruits. Syndicate members disagree over profit, cruelty, loyalty, and how much attention the network can survive.
Recruitment: The Syndicate recruits through payment, debt relief, protection, coercion, family pressure, blackmail, and promises of status. Some minor powered villains join for money or recognition; others are trapped by obligations. Leaving is possible but dangerous, especially for members who know routes, names, finances, or the leader's methods.

Vermine.name: Vermine
Vermine.basicInfo: A morally divided Turned faction that believes humanity's laws, institutions, and ordinary citizens are complicit in the persecution and exploitation of Turned people. Vermine sabotages human systems, attacks selected targets, steals supplies, and uses terror to make humans afraid of what they have created.
Vermine.hiddenInfo: Vermine contains frightened mutual-aid cells, ideological organizers, traumatized survivors, opportunists, and violent extremists. Some members protect vulnerable Turned and avoid civilians; others advocate attacks on human neighborhoods, infrastructure, or symbolic targets. Leadership is fragmented, and not every Vermine operation reflects the same doctrine. The faction seeks Turned materials for survival, medicine, weapons, and illicit upgrades. Negotiation is possible but never guarantees safety or innocence.
